title: Coinbase Beats Frontier Models in Fraud Detection Using Qwen3.5-9B

tickers.name: Coinbase Global, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Internal operational efficiency at the cryptocurrency exchange has increased through the deployment of a specialized artificial intelligence architecture. Coinbase fine-tuned the open weight Qwen3.5-9B model on proprietary data to identify fraudulent activity, outperforming generalist frontier models in both speed and cost for the specific task of fraud prevention.

CEO Brian Armstrong expects other companies to adopt similar specialist models for narrow tasks as they begin to surpass generalist tools. Coinbase has now implemented an internal harness that allows employees to spin up and train their own models, such as those for payments risk review, to eventually replace certain backend services.

selectedTweets.text:
We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.
